Despite headline valuation multiples, Noida Toll Bridge Company Ltd carries severe structural and balance sheet risks that undermine its investment case. The company suffers from an alarming negative Return on Equity of -215.84% against a sector benchmark of 7.69% [E9], alongside a distressed current ratio of 0.51x where current liabilities severely exceed current assets [E33]. Furthermore, long-term wealth creation has been profoundly negative, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -11% [E13], a 10-year profit growth of -12% [E17], and a 10-year share price decline of -15% [E21]. Operational quality is also suspect, with operating cash flow making up only 49% of operating profit in March 2026 [E32], and earnings heavily inflated by ₹16.8 Cr in other income [E56]. While the current ratio stands at 0.51x [E33], the business generated a robust Rs 37 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 36 Cr in free cash flow in March 2026 [E30, E31], completely backing its profits with actual cash [E29]. Long-term sales and profit declines [E13, E17] are firmly in the rearview mirror, having been completely eclipsed by a sharp multi-year turnaround featuring 27% 5-year sales growth [E14] and 40% 3-year profit growth [E19], plus a massive 1365% profit surge in the trailing twelve months [E20]. Finally, the low promoter holding of 26.4% [E55] and declining domestic institutional stake [E38] matter little when the rules-based screen awards the stock a strong 89 out of 100 [E57], backed by a supportive services sector tailwind score of +0.58 [E64].

The bull highlights stellar operational returns via ROCE figures [E10, E12], but glosses over the catastrophic reality that equity holders are being wiped out with a disastrous ROE of -215.84% against a sector benchmark of 7.69% [E9]. Conceded: the business generated Rs 37 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 36 Cr in free cash flow [E30, E31], yet the current ratio sits at a perilous 0.51x where current liabilities severely exceed current assets [E33]. While the bull dismisses long-term declines [E13, E17], the historical record shows compounded share price growth of -15% over 10 years, -7% over 5 years, and -13% over 3 years [E21, E22, E23], proving the market remains unconvinced by any turnaround narrative. The massive 1365% profit surge in the trailing twelve months [E20] requires heavy qualification since earnings explicitly include a suspicious other income component of Rs. 16.8 Cr [E56]. Furthermore, the bull brushes off low promoter holdings [E55], but domestic institutions continue to actively exit the stock, dropping their stake from 0.95% to 0.60% [E38]. Finally, heavy annualised volatility of 58.1% combined with an abysmal Sharpe ratio of 0.24 [E49, E50] demonstrates that holding this asset carries punishing, uncompensated risks far beyond what a surface-level screen score can capture [E57].
